text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) says Zimbabwe has allowed the proliferation of commercial trade in ivory in violation of an international ban on such trade.

- The government has apparently failed to provide a guarantee for the Z$350 million loan offered by the Chinese Import and Export Bank to finance the relining of a major blast furnace at Zimbabwe's steelworks company Zisco, sources told the Financial Gazette.

- A leading proponent of the policy of black economic empowerment says the government should move fast to establish an unlisted securities exchange primarily for small companies to enable them to raise capital for expansion.

- Most of the lodges and tourist facilities under Zimbabwe's Department of Parks and Wildlife Management will soon be run by black business people under a plan being considered to give an added push to their entry into the white-controlled tourism industry.
- At least 2,000 new jobs are expected to be created by nine projects which have been approved by Zimbabwe's Export Processing Zone (EPZ) authority.
- The country's largest building society, Central African Building Society, has introduced telebanking for the first time in Zimbabwe, allowing customers to make transactions over the telephone.

- The government's decision to commercialise its enterprises is beginning to bear fruit, with the Cotton Company of Zimbabwe paying Treasury its first dividend of Z$15 million, reversing a decade-long tradition of receiving state funding for it's operations.
